items.title: Lionel Ferbos Interview, 1964-08-03
items.q: That was after the band you had with Johnny Handy.

ctx.x: to his mouth. No, no, no. I don't want you. You never met him? Just unassumable as can be, but the finest play you ever play? He never smiled. He's a phenomenal. I'm a smart guy. He's a nice fellow. And even one of the fun times we would have, in fact I would have so many different times I wouldn't know exactly when we'd stop working on that because it'd be one place and there'd be another. We'd work at the, what was it, the Papaw? Oh, Decatur Street. Yeah. Papaw and Decatur Street. We worked at the Lake,…

One thing I was going to ask you, it depends. You know, that band you were talking about with Son Johnson, that was at the Entertainers Club. That was after the band you had with Johnny Handy. Yeah. That's right.

That was after. I can tell that for a reason, because I was away with Walter Pichon, I think. And the band was real good. In fact the band was so good it was a shame that they were making the money. But we were playing in the singing theaters. And I got tired of making those trips and getting through, like we were running through Arkansas and so forth. And we'd go through all the mountains and everything, and we didn't even have a chance to even get a chance to eat and I didn't even have to hit the stage and play…
